texts.facts: The notification is erroneous and invoked the writ jurisdiction and the same is passed without hearing the petitioner. The impugned action of the respondents is highly arbitrary illegal perverse and the same is made with malafides. 5.2. That the impugned action of the respondents is violative of Article 300-A of the Constitution of India inasmuch as petitioner is deprived of the land and compensation for subject land. The petitioners/land loser has not received even a penny from the respondents since 30 years of acquisition.
texts.arguments: The declaration of the said land as slum area does not amount to acquisition of the said land. Since the said residential area was not having basic amenities like proper road, electricity, drinking water and drainage facilities, the area was declared as slum in order to develop the area by providing basic necessities and infrastructure. The counsel appearing for the Slum Board also vehemently contend that, by issuing possession certificate only recognized their possession and notification was issued by the Government under Section 3 of the Karnataka Slum Areas (Improvement and Clearance) Act, 1973. The action of the respondents in unilaterally basing on the reports is without jurisdiction and no such provision is available in the Act to de-notify the same. The counsel also relied the judgment of this Court in the case of Smt.P.Nagarathana Vs. The Ningappa S/O Mallappa Walikar vs The State Of Karnataka on 27 September, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/52176162/ 22 So long as possession is not taken over, the mere fact of a notification under Section 4 nor declaration under Section 6 having been made does not divest the owner of his rights in respect of the Ningappa S/O Mallappa Walikar vs The State Of Karnataka on 27 September, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/52176162/ 23 - 27 - NC: 2024:KHC-D:14142 WP No. 101473 of 2023 C/W WP No. 104671 of 2023 land or relieve him of the duty to take care of the land and protect it against encroachments. Hence the contention of the petitioners that there is no any provision under the Act to de-notify the same cannot be accepted. 18.
